sp_widget.description: Custom unauthenticated Service Portal widget for case status lookup. Renders a single case-number input field plus a Look Up Status button, GETs /api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup, and displays ONLY the whitelisted fields { status, subject, opened_date } on match or the verbatim text 'No case found with that number.' on no-match per AAP Section 0.7.4. Embedded by sp_page_x_casemgmt_case_status. No internal fields (assigned_group, assigned_agent, description, closed_date, requester_name, requester_email, priority, type, pending_reason, audit fields) are exposed. Every 4xx (404 not-found, 400 bad-request) renders the same verbatim no-case-found message, so no case-number enumeration oracle exists; a 5xx, a network failure or an expired 20-second client deadline renders a separate 'service could not be reached' panel instead, because in those cases nothing was learned about the case and the verbatim message would be false. Replaces ArkCase's GetCaseByNumberServiceImpl.getCaseByNumber() and PortalRequestService.getRequestStatus() Spring services. No client-side or server-side database operations - all data flows through the scripted REST endpoint. Per AAP Sections 0.4.3, 0.4.4, 0.5.1, and 0.7.4 (verbatim no-case-found message) and Validation Gate 5 (Portal - lookup).
sp_widget.name: Case Lookup Widget
sp_widget.script:
(function() { /* * Case Lookup Widget - server-side data initialization. * * No case data is fetched here. The case-status lookup is driven * entirely by the client-side controller via $http.get to the * scripted REST endpoint at * /api/x_casemgmt/case_status_lookup?number=<encoded> * defined by ../rest/sys_ws_definition_x_casemgmt_case_status_lookup.xml * and handled by ../rest/sys_ws_operation_x_casemgmt_case_status_lookup_get.xml. * * This widget performs ZERO database operations: * - No GlideRecord reads (no pre-fetching of any case data; the * widget renders with empty state and the user drives the * lookup via the form). * - No GlideRecord writes (the lookup is read-only by definition; * all writes in this scoped application go through the * scripted REST endpoints, never through widget server scripts). * - No gs.eventQueue() calls (email notifications are disabled * per AAP Section 0.7.2 Email-disabled constraint). * * It computes exactly TWO values, neither of which reads the case * table: the name of the timezone that the Opened Date on the result * panel is expressed in, and the case number this page was reached * with when it was reached from a submission confirmation. Each is * explained at its assignment below. * * WHY THE LABEL LIVES HERE AND NOT IN THE LOOKUP RESPONSE. * x_casemgmt.CasePortalService.lookupCase() emits the opened_date * DISPLAY value, rendered in the session's timezone, so the external * requester and internal staff read the same instant. An unlabelled * local timestamp is still ambiguous to a requester in another * timezone, but the lookup response cannot carry the label: AAP * Section 0.7.4 fixes that payload at EXACTLY three keys (status, * subject, opened_date) and a fourth would widen a whitelist the * specification pins shut. The widget therefore resolves the label * from its own session - the same session whose timezone the display * value was rendered in, because the anonymous $http.get below is * issued by this same portal visitor - and renders it beside the * field's <dt> label rather than beside the value, so it reads as * part of the label and never as case data. * * getTimeZoneName() is read defensively: an empty string is the * expected outcome on an instance with no default timezone property, * and the template simply omits the qualifier in that case rather * than rendering an empty pair of parentheses. The try/catch bounds * a session API that an anonymous request is not guaranteed to be * able to answer; a missing label degrades the panel by nothing more * than the qualifier. */ data.openedDateTimeZone = ''; try { var sessionTimeZone = gs.getSession().getTimeZoneName(); if (sessionTimeZone) { data.openedDateTimeZone = String(sessionTimeZone); } } catch (e) { gs.warn('x_casemgmt Case Lookup Widget: session timezone name unavailable, ' + 'the Opened Date qualifier will be omitted; ' + e); }
/* * The case number this page was reached WITH, when it was reached from * a confirmation. * * The submission confirmation links here as * ?id=x_casemgmt_case_status&number=CASE0000001 * (see ../widgets/sp_widget_x_casemgmt_case_confirmation_widget.xml). * Without this, the requester followed a link labelled "Check the * status of this case", landed on an empty form, and had to re-type * the number the link they had just clicked already carried - which is * most of the friction the link was added to remove. * * The value is treated as untrusted input from the address bar, so it * is trimmed and capped at the 20 characters the input's own maxlength * allows. It is never used to build a query here: it only pre-fills * c.caseNumber, and the lookup still goes through the same * encodeURIComponent'd GET to the same anonymous endpoint, which * queries by the number field and answers 404 for anything it does * not recognise. It reaches the template through ng-model, which * renders it as a value and never as markup, so a crafted parameter * has nothing to act on. * * An absent parameter yields '' and the page behaves exactly as it * did: empty field, no request, user drives the lookup. */ data.prefilledNumber = ''; var suppliedNumber = $sp.getParameter('number'); if (suppliedNumber) { data.prefilledNumber = String(suppliedNumber).trim().substring(0, 20); } })();
